title: Cuba goodwill trip: playing trombone in a funeral band
summary: On a New Orleans goodwill tour to Havana the Straws marched in carnival as a blackface Negro funeral band, Zanco on trombone; they played Didn't He Ramble and the Saints.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. You started playing, I believe, if I'll refresh your memory, you played trombone on a game you made in Cuba.

Yeah. Yeah. I forgot about it. Oh, I'm also a trombone. You didn't know that. That was in May, wasn't it? I think so, yeah. We went to Cuba with the group and Joe was still here. So I played the trombone on the trip. And I don't think I'll ever see my name up in lights, but I must say it sounded pretty good.
Yeah, I made it anyway, playing the trombone. I guess I'd have played the comb, the silk paper and comb to make that trip to Cuba, you know. I was willing to play anything.
What was it like down there?

That was a fine trip. What it was, it was a goodwill tour from the city of New Orleans. And they just happened to pick our group to go. And all the 11th quarters, we stayed in this Havana Hilton. That's one of the finest hotels in Cuba. And they really treated us like kings while we were there. We had a good time. We marched in a parade. They were in this, you see, they had this, oh, this big carnival of Cuba in Havana. And we marched in a parade and we had to use this blackface routine to represent a Negro funeral band. You see. The musicians were kind of half dead anyway, so we made a pretty good funeral band.
What tunes did you play as a funeral band?

Well, we played Didn't He Ramble, Just a Little While to Stay Here. We kind of jazzed up a version on Closer Walk with D. We played the Saints. and I think we more or less repeated the same tunes over and over, you know, parade stuff, you know.
Did you play a slow tune for a funeral, before the funeral?
No, we just went right into the marching routine, you know, we had to put more of a march beat to them, but those are supposedly Negro funeral tunes, that's the kind of stuff they played.
I mean, you played them as a, you were a coming back band.
A coming back band, that's it, yeah.
